assertion.hypothesis_label: Vascular and Blood-Brain Barrier Clearance Model
assertion.description: Cerebral blood flow changes, neurovascular-unit injury, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and impaired amyloid-beta clearance are modeled as causal or reinforcing contributors to Alzheimer disease progression.
assertion.notes: Retained as ALTERNATIVE. The mechanistic evidence is strong and now molecular (APOE4-graded pericyte degeneration through cyclophilin A and MMP-9, PICALM linking the two endothelial clearance routes, hypoperfusion raising amyloid in a transgenic model), but the human causal proof is missing: no interventional trial has shown that correcting vascular dysfunction prevents or slows amyloid accumulation, and the rrAD trial (NCT02913664) is pending with neurocognitive rather than serial amyloid PET primary outcomes. The model's reach is also bounded at tau — see the vascular-to-tau knowledge gap. Assessed from the OpenScientist vascular_bbb_clearance_model report; that report's ARIA-E incidence figure of 22-36% is not in the Cochrane review it cites (PMID:41985900 reports an absolute risk difference of 107 more per 1000) and was deliberately not curated, nor was its CL:0000669 lead, which names the pericyte cell type rather than pericyte death.

assertion.description: Amyloid-beta production, oligomerization, and plaque deposition are modeled as upstream drivers of tau pathology, synaptic toxicity, glial activation, and progressive cognitive decline, especially in APP/PSEN-associated familial Alzheimer disease.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL, but not sufficient as a complete disease explanation: tau burden, vascular injury, immune state, lysosomal clearance, aging, and genetic background modulate how amyloid pathology maps to symptoms. Best read as a necessary rather than sufficient initiating trigger, applying most strongly to familial disease and to the amyloid-first sporadic subtype. Four independent lines qualify it and are curated above: a tau-first spatiotemporal subtype (PMID:37433038), the Cochrane finding that amyloid removal produces no clinically meaningful benefit (PMID:41985900), oldest-old resilience attributable to co-pathology rather than amyloid tolerance (PMID:41942821), and an APP-dependent C99 endolysosomal arm that does not run through amyloid-beta (PMID:31043483). assertion.description: Synapse loss — the pathological change that correlates best with cognitive decline — is modeled as an active, receptor-mediated phagocytic process rather than as passive degeneration secondary to amyloid or tau toxicity. The classical complement cascade that prunes surplus synapses during development (C1q tagging, C3 opsonization, microglial CR3 engagement) is modeled as being reactivated early in disease, so that microglia engulf structurally intact synapses. Soluble amyloid-beta oligomers and phosphorylated tau both act as upstream triggers, which makes this the mechanism by which two otherwise separate proteinopathies converge on the same cellular endpoint.
assertion.notes: ALTERNATIVE rather than CANONICAL. The necessity evidence (C1q, C3 and CR3 blockade) is entirely mouse; the same paper that supplies the best human evidence for glial synapse ingestion states that direct human evidence for glial involvement in synapse removal remained to be established, and implicates MFG-E8 rather than complement. Curated as a distinct hypothesis group rather than folded into neuroimmune_glial_amplification_model because it makes a specific, falsifiable claim about a named cascade acting on a named substrate (the synapse), and because its therapeutic prediction — anti-C1q antibody — is being tested clinically. See the attached HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion before strengthening the human claim.

assertion.description: SARS-CoV-2-associated immune perturbation permits reactivation of latent herpesviruses, especially EBV and possibly CMV/VZV, which may then amplify inflammatory, fatigue, and neurocognitive Long COVID phenotypes.
assertion.notes: Added for GitHub issue 3664. Current support is strongest for EBV serology in post-acute cohorts and for review-level latent-infection framing; whether VZV reactivation is an independent Long COVID driver rather than an acute/post-acute complication remains unresolved. Retained as EMERGING per the 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Long_COVID/herpesvirus_reactivation_model); verdict PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (96 papers reviewed, 16 findings confirmed). The EBV-Long COVID reactivation-serology association is one of the most replicated findings in the field (6+ independent cohorts; meta-analytic OR ~6.45 for active EBV in severe COVID-19), extends to CMV/HHV-6, maps onto fatigue- and cognition-dominant subtypes, and persists even after mild COVID (Karachaliou n=1083, PMID:39247972). Four qualifications prevent upgrade to SUPPORTED: (1) a consistent serology-viremia dissociation - reactivation antibody markers are elevated but ongoing viremia is usually undetectable, raising bystander B-cell activation rather than productive replication as an alternative; (2) no RCT of anti-herpesviral therapy in Long COVID (only open-label pilots and an indirect ME/CFS valganciclovir RCT); (3) complete absence of in vitro or animal-model evidence for the SARS-CoV-2 -> herpesvirus reactivation trigger itself; and (4) non-replication in some cohorts (large German PCS case-control study PMID:39847575 found no discriminating EBV markers; a Brazilian cohort was negative) plus non-COVID-specificity (comparable herpesvirus reactivation rates in non-COVID sepsis/critical illness, PMID:24919177).

assertion.description: Persistent viral RNA/antigen reservoirs sustain immune activation and downstream multisystem dysfunction, providing the default explanatory framework for Long COVID.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL but partially supported per the 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Long_COVID/canonical_persistence_immune_model). 79 papers reviewed. Three critical qualifications: (1) the PAX LC randomized controlled trial of nirmatrelvir-ritonavir showed no significant benefit on the primary outcome, suggesting that eliminating replicating virus is insufficient to reverse established Long COVID; (2) downstream pathologies (autoimmunity, endothelial senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, serotonin depletion) appear self-sustaining once initiated; (3) large-scale phenotyping reveals mechanistically distinct patient subtypes that cannot all be explained by a single upstream trigger. Best understood as the primary *initiating* mechanism within a multi-pathway framework requiring subtype-stratified therapeutic approaches. Peluso and Deeks 2024 (PMID:39326415) is cited as the current synthesis supporting an experimental-medicine and clinical-trials agenda for this multi-mechanism framing.

assertion.description: SARS-CoV-2 triggers de novo autoantibody production through B-cell dysregulation, molecular mimicry, and bystander activation, contributing to multisystem symptoms and immune-mediated tissue damage in Long COVID.
assertion.notes: Retained as EMERGING per the 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Long_COVID/autoimmune_model). Strongly supported molecular pathways (extrafollicular B-cell activation, molecular mimicry, bystander activation) and a 2026 passive transfer study (PMID:42053865) showing pathogenic IgG from Long COVID patients induces pain/sensory symptoms in mice. Three critical caveats: (1) persistence debated — many autoantibodies decline by 12 months (e.g., anti-apoA-1 from 93% to 15%); (2) passive transfer reproduced pain/sensory hypersensitivity but explicitly failed to induce cognitive/mood/memory deficits, excluding the most prevalent Long COVID symptoms from the autoantibody hypothesis; (3) no completed RCT has demonstrated that removing autoantibodies improves Long COVID. Most plausibly applies to pain-dominant and cardiopulmonary phenotypes as one component of multifactorial pathogenesis.

assertion.description: Persistent gut microbiota dysbiosis following SARS-CoV-2 infection disrupts gut-lung and gut-brain axis homeostasis, contributing to systemic immune dysregulation and neurological manifestations.
assertion.notes: Retained as EMERGING per the 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Long_COVID/microbiome_dysbiosis_model). 69 papers reviewed. Correlative evidence is robust: at least five independent cohorts demonstrate persistent gut dysbiosis (reduced alpha diversity, SCFA-producer depletion, opportunistic-pathogen enrichment). Wong et al. (2023, Cell) provides a complete mechanistic chain: viral persistence → IFN-driven impaired tryptophan absorption → peripheral serotonin reduction → impaired vagal/hippocampal function. SIM01 synbiotic RCT (Lau 2024) provides preliminary interventional support. **Critical directional challenge:** Wang et al. (2026, Developmental Cell) demonstrate that intestinal SARS-CoV-2 reservoirs directly cause microbiota dysbiosis via VLCFA-peroxisome impairment of epithelial regeneration — reframing dysbiosis as a downstream amplifier rather than an independent upstream driver. Augustin et al. (2026) confirm viral proteins in GALT 15-22 months post-infection. Best understood as a secondary amplifier within the multifactorial framework, with strongest explanatory power for GI-predominant and neurocognitive subtypes.

assertion.description: Interferon-linked serotonin depletion impairs vagal signaling and hippocampal responses, contributing to cognitive and autonomic symptoms.
assertion.notes: Retained as EMERGING per the 2026 falcon hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Long_COVID/serotonin_vagal_model). Most compelling mechanistic chain is from Wong et al. (2023, Cell): viral persistence → type I interferon-driven inflammation → impaired intestinal tryptophan absorption → reduced peripheral serotonin → impaired vagal/hippocampal function. The model integrates with the microbiome-dysbiosis hypothesis (shared interferon-tryptophan-serotonin axis) and provides a candidate mechanism for cognitive and autonomic symptoms in oligosymptomatic and pain-dominant subtypes. Definitive validation requires controlled trials of tryptophan repletion or SSRI/5-HT receptor agonist therapy in mechanistically stratified cohorts.

assertion.description: Altered GNAS-dependent signaling in bone and mesenchymal lineages drives brachydactyly, ectopic ossification, and related AHO structural phenotypes.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL per the 2026 falcon hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Pseudohypoparathyroidism/aho_mesenchymal_model; openscientist timed out). assertion.description: Neurologic symptoms, including tetany and seizures, arise primarily from downstream hypocalcemia and associated mineral imbalance.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL per the 2026 falcon hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Pseudohypoparathyroidism/neurohypocalcemia_model; openscientist timed out). assertion.description: Historical but still supported superimposed model proposing that mutant huntingtin and corticostriatal circuit dysfunction enhance NMDA receptor-mediated excitotoxicity in striatal medium spiny neurons. This hypothesis is best viewed as a selective-vulnerability amplifier rather than the sole initiating lesion.
assertion.notes: Retained as ALTERNATIVE. The 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Huntington_Disease/alternative_excitotoxicity) supplies the mechanistic content this framing previously asserted without evidence, and three qualifications a curator should preserve. (1) The proximate lesion is not a global rise in glutamate signalling but a cell-autonomous redistribution of GluN2B-containing NMDA receptors from synaptic to extrasynaptic sites in medium spiny neurons, driven by calpain cleavage of the GluN2B C-terminus and elevated STEP activity and amplified by DAPK1 phosphorylation of GluN2B S1303 - now curated as its own pathophysiology node. (2) The hypothesis is bounded in time. Corticostriatal glutamate release becomes undetectable in HD mice, so excitotoxicity cannot account for neurodegeneration once disconnection has occurred. (3) The human evidence is thin and partly adverse: postmortem in-situ hybridization finds NMDAR subunit mRNA falling with disease severity and reads the astrocytic GLT1 response as compensatory; HD onset-modifier GWAS return mismatch-repair genes and no glutamate-receptor-pathway signal; and NMDA receptor antagonists have failed advanced trials in HD. This human/model gap is recorded as the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion mismatch_hd_extrasynaptic_nmdar_is_mouse_only. Two of the report's leads were not curated: it cites PMID:11554551 (a 2001 review that says the remacemide HD trial was still ongoing) for trial failure, and asserts a modest memantine benefit in HD that neither cited source reports.

selected_evidence.snippet: At both 6 months and 1 yr, QA lesions showed striking sparing of NADPH-diaphorase neurons as compared with both AMPA and KA lesions, neither of which showed preferential sparing of these neurons.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Double-Strand Break Accumulation as an Expansion-Independent Driver
assertion.description: Genome-wide DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are a driver of HD neuropathology that is mechanistically separable from somatic CAG expansion. On this model the two forms of DNA damage coexist but act through distinct routes: site-specific CAG tract lengthening is driven by active mismatch repair, whereas DSBs arise genome-wide from mutant huntingtin-mediated suppression of non-homologous end joining acting on a background where oxidation converts base excision repair single-strand break intermediates into double-strand breaks. Three observations support separability. (1) DSBs accumulate in zQ175/MSH3(-/-) mice, which cannot somatically expand their allele, alongside the same transcriptional dysfunction seen in expansion-competent zQ175. (2) Pharmacological suppression of DSBs with the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant XJB-5-131 rescues striatal neuron loss and motor performance in HdhQ(150/150) mice while leaving somatic tract length substantially unchanged. (3) Geometry - the CAG tract is under 1e-7 of the genome, so most breaks fall outside it, and Ku70/Ku80 limits end-joining length changes inside it to a few nucleotides, so break burden and tract length are largely decoupled. The therapeutic implication is that expansion suppression and DSB suppression are independent targets that may need to be combined.
assertion.notes: Recorded as EMERGING rather than CANONICAL or ALTERNATIVE. It does not displace the canonical toxic gain-of-function or somatic-expansion models; it adds a parallel arm. Four caveats a curator should preserve. (a) All primary evidence is mouse and, in HdhQ(150/150), male only. (b) The DSBR deficit is measured as delayed clearance of radiation-induced breaks rather than as endogenous repair kinetics. (c) XJB-5-131 suppresses DSB formation upstream via mitochondrial reactive oxygen species; it does not restore end joining, so the rescue shows that break burden matters, not that NHEJ was repaired. (d) No DSBR or NHEJ gene has emerged from human HD GWAS, which the authors attribute to breaks being randomly distributed and NHEJ being reduced rather than absent - this remains an unresolved human/model discrepancy, recorded as the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion mismatch_hd_dsbr_absent_from_human_gwas.

selected_evidence.snippet: This had no effect on the deposition of huntingtin aggregation in the nuclei of striatal neurons, nor on the dysregulated striatal transcriptional profile.

assertion.description: Mutant huntingtin disrupts transcriptional regulation by interfering with key transcription factors and co-activators (Sp1/TAFII130, CBP, TBP, REST/NRSF), leading to widespread downregulation of neuronal survival genes including BDNF. This is a canonical downstream mechanistic layer in HD, linking mutant huntingtin protein interactions to loss of neuronal maintenance programs. The interference is now understood as functional inhibition by soluble and oligomeric mutant huntingtin - which structurally destabilizes its target - rather than physical trapping of transcription factors inside visible inclusions; the REST/NRSF arm is separate again, and turns on loss of the wild-type protein's cytoplasmic retention of the repressor.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL, but the mechanism statement was corrected. The 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Huntington_Disease/canonical_transcriptional_dysregulation) surfaced the study that tested the sequestration model directly and did not confirm it: TBP, CBP and Sp1 are diffusely distributed in HD mouse nuclei despite abundant inclusions, and are not trapped in them (PMID:11971872). The resolution is that soluble species do the damage (PMID:15225551), which is also what the entry's own Sp1 evidence says - Sp1 binds soluble, not aggregated, mutant huntingtin. Three further points a curator should keep. (1) The arms are not equally supported: REST/NRSF has genome-wide occupancy data in human postmortem brain plus a loss-of-function phenocopy, Sp1 has human presymptomatic detection plus rescue, and the CBP arm is genuinely contested - recorded as the CONTROVERSY discussion controversy_hd_cbp_depletion_versus_functional_inhibition. (2) Epigenetic silencing runs alongside the transcription-factor arms, and HDAC3 inhibition unexpectedly suppresses striatal CAG expansion as well as correcting gene expression, so the epigenetic layer is not strictly downstream of somatic instability. (3) Therapeutic translation has been poor: no positive phase II or III result for an HDAC inhibitor in HD, and the BET bromodomain inhibitor JQ1 was actively harmful in R6/2 mice while improving wild-type controls. Not integrated from the report: its claim that mitochondrial deficits at postnatal day 0 precede transcriptional change, which rests on a spatial transcriptomics study whose mitochondrial readout is itself transcriptional.

assertion.description: Mutant huntingtin impairs mitochondrial function through reduced oxidative phosphorylation complex activity, disrupted calcium homeostasis, and transcriptional repression of PGC-1alpha. This is a canonical convergent mechanism in HD that links transcriptional dysregulation and mutant huntingtin stress to bioenergetic failure, oxidative damage, and neuronal death, particularly in energy-demanding striatal medium spiny neurons.
assertion.notes: Retained as CANONICAL but reframed as a **downstream convergent mediator** rather than an independent initiating event. The 2026 openscientist hypothesis-search report (kb/hypotheses/Huntington_Disease/canonical_mitochondrial_bioenergetic_failure) reviewed 76 papers and identified three refinements: (1) the transcriptional-repression-of-PGC-1α pathway (PMID:17018277) is the strongest mechanistic link, validated by genetic and rescue experiments; (2) the "direct mHTT-mitochondria interaction" model is challenged by isolated-mitochondria studies, shifting emphasis toward indirect transcription-mediated mechanisms; (3) GWAS overwhelmingly implicate DNA-repair/somatic-expansion genes — not mitochondrial genes — as rate-limiting modifiers, positioning mitochondrial dysfunction as a downstream amplifier rather than an upstream driver. assertion.hypothesis_label: Excess of natural anticoagulants (free TFPI-alpha, activated protein C)
assertion.description: Bleeding is caused by an excess of physiological anticoagulants rather than by any procoagulant deficiency. Free TFPI-alpha above the 95th percentile is over-represented specifically in the unexplained-bleeding subgroup, TFPI activity is raised in a subset of an independent unclassified-bleeding cohort, and activated protein C antigen is highest in BDUC. Attractive because it reconciles a normal factor panel with a damped thrombin burst, and because it is the only candidate arm whose authors have proposed a concrete therapeutic target.

selected_evidence.snippet: For patients with BDUC, further evaluation may include non-routine testing to look for rare bleeding disorders not detected by routine hemostasis tests, such as thrombomodulin-associated coagulopathy, tissue factor pathway inhibitor-related bleeding disorder, hyperfibrinolytic-bleeding disorders or impaired tissue factor production.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Occult platelet function or secretion defect below assay resolution
assertion.description: Bleeding is caused by a platelet activation, secretion, or receptor-signaling defect that light transmission aggregometry cannot resolve. Supported indirectly by the acknowledged reproducibility limits of aggregometry and directly by immature-platelet receptor profiling and platelet lipidomics — both of which, importantly, were performed in patients with abnormal aggregometry rather than in formally defined BDUC, so their transfer to BDUC is assumed rather than shown.

selected_evidence.snippet: The etiology of bleeding is postulated to be due to defects in platelet function, fibrinolysis, collagen integrity, and/or other coagulation defects not well measured in standard laboratory assays.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Soluble thrombomodulin excess as a cause of unexplained bleeding
assertion.description: A specific and testable proposal, derived from families with THBD variants causing massively raised soluble thrombomodulin, that the same mechanism underlies unexplained mild bleeding more broadly. It is curated here precisely because it was tested and failed: in 507 patients with mild bleeding disorders including BUC, soluble thrombomodulin levels, their distribution, their relationship to bleeding severity, and THBD sequencing were all unremarkable. Retained as DEPRECATED rather than deleted so that the negative result is visible and the hypothesis is not silently re-proposed.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Obstructive sleep apnea-associated chronic intermittent hypoxia as a progression driver
assertion.description: Chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) — the cyclical desaturation-reoxygenation of obstructive sleep apnea — is proposed to act on the liver as a second hit that is separable from adiposity, upregulating SREBP-1/SCD-1-dependent hepatic lipogenesis and generating hepatic lipid peroxidation, and thereby accelerating the transition from steatosis to steatohepatitis and fibrosis. This is deliberately modeled as a parallel arm of the pathograph rather than a replacement for the canonical lipotoxic backbone, and as EMERGING rather than CANONICAL, for three reasons that the curated evidence states directly. (1) The human data are observational, and they do not agree with each other endpoint by endpoint: the largest individual-participant meta-analysis attributes the fibrosis association mainly to body mass index by causal mediation analysis while finding apnea severity an independent risk factor for steatosis, whereas the one cohort scored on liver biopsy inverts that pattern, finding an obesity-adjusted fibrosis association but no association with steatosis or steatohepatitis. Each edge therefore carries both the supporting and the refuting human result. (2) The causal, dose-controlled experiments — including the HIF-1 dependence of the triglyceride response — are five-day murine intermittent-hypoxia exposures in lean mice, a model that produced no additional effect in already-obese mice. (3) Correcting the exposure does not correct the liver: randomized trials of CPAP monotherapy show no change in steatosis, fibrosis or aminotransferases. A curator extending this arm should preserve that asymmetry rather than resolving it, and should not curate CPAP as a MASLD therapy.

selected_evidence.snippet: We conclude that 1) the effect of IH on serum TG levels is mediated through HIF-1, 2) HIF-1 may impact on posttranscriptional regulation of SREBP-1

assertion.hypothesis_label: Liver sinusoidal endothelial dysfunction as an early driver
assertion.description: An endothelium-first model in which loss of the liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) phenotype — capillarization (loss of fenestrae) and loss of shear-responsive vasodilator production — occurs early, before overt steatohepatitis, and then licenses inflammatory-cell recruitment and hepatic stellate cell activation rather than merely following hepatocyte injury. This is deliberately modeled as a parallel arm of the pathograph, not a replacement for the canonical lipotoxic backbone: the human data are cross-sectional histology, and the causal experiments are endothelium-specific mouse models. The same endothelial lesion has been proposed as the axis shared with atherosclerosis, where vascular endothelial dysfunction initiates lipoprotein retention and leukocyte recruitment; whether dismech should represent that shared axis as a cross-disease module or a comorbidity entry is an open scope question (issue #6352), so no cross-disease structure is asserted here.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Transporter-mediated hepatic fatty acid uptake as a rate-limiting, druggable step
assertion.description: The canonical model treats the hepatocyte as a passive sink for the non-esterified fatty acid load that adipose insulin resistance releases. This hypothesis holds instead that entry into the hepatocyte is itself protein-mediated and rate-limiting, so that the fatty acid transport proteins on the basolateral hepatocyte membrane — FATP5 (SLC27A5), which is expressed exclusively by liver, and FATP2 (SLC27A2) — set how much of that load actually reaches the hepatic lipid pool, and blocking them reverses steatosis that is already established. The strong form of the claim is therapeutic: hepatic fatty acid uptake is a target in its own right, upstream of and separable from the lipogenic and oxidative arms the approved agents act on. It is modeled as EMERGING, not canonical, for two reasons the curated evidence states directly. First, every causal experiment is murine knockdown or knockout; no FATP-directed agent has been tested in human MASLD, and no human genetic evidence linking SLC27A5 or SLC27A2 variation to MASLD is curated here. Second, hepatic FATP5 knockdown also reduced whole-animal caloric uptake, so the reported protection is not cleanly attributable to the hepatic uptake step alone — a confound the source paper reports rather than one imputed to it. A curator strengthening this arm should look for the human evidence that is missing, not for more rodent replication.

selected_evidence.snippet: Our findings support the hypothesis that efficient hepatocellular uptake of LCFAs, and thus liver lipid homeostasis in general, is largely a protein-mediated process requiring FATP5.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Fbw7-degron stabilisation as a dosage-restoration strategy
assertion.description: If SCF-Fbw7-mediated turnover sets the steady-state level of MED13 protein, then slowing turnover of the product of the intact allele in a haploinsufficient cell could raise MED13 toward the diploid level and restore CKM occupancy. This is the one route from MED13 mechanism to a candidate therapeutic handle. The major caveat is target selectivity: FBXW7 is a broadly acting tumour suppressor, so non-selective inhibition of its ligase activity carries oncogenic risk and any viable strategy would need to spare its other substrates.

selected_evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that FBXW7 is inactivated by mutation in diverse human cancer types with an overall mutation frequency of approximately 6%.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Clustered missense variants act by altered function rather than simple dosage loss
assertion.description: Pathogenic MED13 missense variants cluster in two small regions — an N-terminal region containing the Thr326/Pro327 SCF-Fbw7 phosphodegron and a C-terminal region — plus a central pair of residues around 834/835. The clustering itself argues against simple loss of function, which would tolerate variants anywhere. Clinically, the most severe reported presentations (developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, neonatal multi-organ disease with mitochondrial pathology) have so far occurred with missense rather than truncating alleles. Degron-region variants are predicted to stabilise MED13 against Fbw7-mediated turnover, which would raise rather than lower CKM occupancy. This is structured inference from position and phenotype; no functional assay has yet demonstrated altered function for any MED13 missense allele.
assertion.notes: Kept as EMERGING rather than CANONICAL, and explicitly contested. The clustering and severity signals are real, but no functional data distinguish altered function from a severe hypomorph, ClinGen's expert-panel curation across the full allelic series concluded loss of function, and the same p.Pro835Ser allele has been reported with quite different clinical courses.

selected_evidence.snippet: The mechanism of pathogenicity is loss of function.

assertion.hypothesis_label: The cardiac miR-208a/MED13 metabolic axis as a systemic-phenotype modifier
assertion.description: In mice, cardiac MED13 acts through nuclear-receptor signalling to control systemic energy expenditure: cardiac MED13 overexpression or miR-208a inhibition confers resistance to diet-induced obesity, while cardiomyocyte MED13 deletion worsens it. If this axis is dosage-sensitive in humans, it offers a candidate explanation for the restricted growth reported in a subset of MRD61 patients that is independent of the neurodevelopmental phenotype, and predicts that variant class might track with growth and cardiac trajectory. No human data test this.
assertion.notes: Entirely murine. The human MRD61 growth phenotype is restricted growth rather than obesity, so the direction of any human effect is not established; this is a hypothesis about a candidate modifier axis, not a claimed mechanism.

If this axis is dosage-sensitive in humans, it offers a candidate explanation for the restricted growth reported in a subset of MRD61 patients that is independent of the neurodevelopmental phenotype, and predicts that variant class might track with growth and cardiac trajectory. No human data test this.
assertion.notes: Entirely murine. The human MRD61 growth phenotype is restricted growth rather than obesity, so the direction of any human effect is not established; this is a hypothesis about a candidate modifier axis, not a claimed mechanism.

selected_evidence.snippet: Cardiac-specific overexpression of MED13 or pharmacologic inhibition of miR-208a in mice confers resistance to high-fat diet-induced obesity and improves systemic insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance.

assertion.hypothesis_label: MED13 haploinsufficiency as the mechanism for truncating alleles
assertion.description: Heterozygous truncating MED13 variants and whole-gene 17q23.2 deletions reduce the pool of CDK8 kinase module available to dock on core Mediator. Supported by the predominance of de novo truncating alleles in the founding cohort, by an independent whole-gene deletion phenocopy, and by the explicit haploinsufficiency conclusion drawn from a functionally characterised frameshift case.

selected_evidence.snippet: This case is also consistent with haploinsufficiency as the disease mechanism for truncating MED13 variants in MRD61, underscoring the importance of exome sequencing in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders and congenital anomalies.

assertion.description: Primary insulin resistance or primary hyperinsulinemia initiates the endocrine-metabolic loop. High insulin acts as a co-gonadotropin in the ovary and lowers hepatic SHBG, increasing bioactive androgen exposure; the resulting hyperandrogenism can then worsen insulin resistance and adiposity.
assertion.notes: OpenScientist deep-research verdict (see kb/hypotheses/Polycystic_Ovary_Syndrome/insulin_hyperinsulinemia_first_model): PARTIALLY SUPPORTED — a co-driving parallel pathway rather than a universal primary cause, so `status:` stays ALTERNATIVE. What survives source check: suppressing insulin secretion with diazoxide lowers androgens and raises SHBG even in lean PCOS women with normal metabolic insulin sensitivity (PMID:17559844); insulin drives adipose androgen generation through AKR1C3 (PMID:26312838); and Mendelian randomization infers a causal effect of higher insulin resistance on PCOS risk (PMID:26416764). What does not: the report's claim that PCOS GWAS do not implicate insulin genes and that no insulin-specific Mendelian-randomization work exists is contradicted by that same 2015 analysis and by the INSR locus already curated in `genetic:`; its claimed insulin-independent 28-52% testosterone contrast across two NK3-antagonist trials misreports those endpoints (52% was the LH area-under-curve reduction in the AZD4901 trial); and average null gonadotropin effects in a heterogeneous metformin meta-analysis do not prove parallel causal pathways. Note also that metformin lowers LH-stimulated testosterone within days, before any insulin-sensitising effect (PMID:25304843), so therapeutic response to an insulin sensitiser is not on its own evidence for the insulin-first ordering.

selected_evidence.snippet: Insulin functions as a co-gonadotropin through its cognate receptor to modulate ovarian steroidogenesis.

assertion.description: Intrinsic ovarian/adrenal androgen excess, potentially reinforced by heightened LH action and theca-cell steroidogenic machinery, is the initiating lesion. Androgen excess then promotes insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia, disrupts hypothalamic steroid feedback, and contributes to visceral adiposity, closing an androgen-insulin-adiposity feedback loop.

The androgen-sensitive ovarian and neuroendocrine components are supported — global and neuron-specific androgen-receptor knockout in the DHT mouse model shows that androgen-receptor signalling is required for the PCOS-like phenotype and that its critical locus is extraovarian (PMID:28320971) — but temporal primacy of androgen excess is not demonstrated in humans, so `status:` stays ALTERNATIVE rather than being promoted. Three qualifications from the assessment (assessments/openscientist-assessment-by-codex.yaml) are carried here. (1) The report's central argument that androgen reduction leaves insulin resistance unchanged was rejected on source check: it reads a 12-month placebo-controlled flutamide trial that reported *improved* insulin sensitivity as null, so no claim of a purely indirect androgen-to-insulin route is curated here; see the discussion gap_pcos_androgen_to_insulin_resistance_directness. assertion.hypothesis_label: Canonical HEXA Deficiency / GM2 Ganglioside Neuronal Storage Model
assertion.description: Biallelic pathogenic HEXA variants impair the alpha subunit of lysosomal HexA, an alpha/beta heterodimer requiring the GM2 activator protein for membrane GM2 hydrolysis. Deficient catabolism causes neuronal GM2 storage, followed by neuronal dysfunction and loss, glial inflammation and variable myelin abnormalities. Residual activity shapes a continuum from infantile to juvenile and late-onset disease. The downstream contributions of ER stress, autophagy and neurodevelopmental perturbation require context-specific interpretation. Mouse neuraminidase bypass metabolism limits translation from Hexa-null animals.
assertion.notes: The core mechanism remains canonical. OpenScientist correctly identified the Hexa/Neu3 mouse-model correction and several experimental downstream mechanisms, but overstated HSCT causal inference and missed published human AAV results and fetal-brain transcriptomics. Human biochemical target engagement does not ensure clinical benefit; the report is assessed separately against primary studies.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Relative cholinergic deficiency with dopaminergic excess
assertion.description: The oldest mechanistic account of delirium, motivated by the deliriogenic potency of anticholinergic and dopaminergic drugs. It is retained here as ALTERNATIVE rather than CANONICAL because its two strongest predictions have failed. Therapeutically, augmenting cholinergic transmission with rivastigmine did not shorten delirium in critically ill patients and the trial was stopped early for excess mortality in the treatment arm; and dopamine-receptor blockade with haloperidol or ziprasidone did not alter delirium duration against placebo. The neurotransmitter disturbance is real and is the best explanation for drug-precipitated delirium; what the negative trials refute is that correcting it downstream reverses the syndrome.

selected_evidence.snippet: Impaired cholinergic neurotransmission seems to have an important role in the development of delirium.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Delirium as the product of baseline vulnerability multiplied by an acute precipitant
assertion.description: The multifactorial model is the organizing framework for delirium and the one this entry's pathograph is built on: predisposing factors (age, dementia, frailty, sensory impairment) set the threshold, and precipitating insults (infection, surgery, drugs, metabolic derangement) cross it. Its strength is that it explains why a trivial insult suffices in one patient and a series of major ones is needed in another, and why single-target interventions fail while multicomponent ones work. Its weakness as a *mechanistic* model is that it is a risk architecture rather than a molecular pathway — it says which combinations produce delirium, not what the brain does when they do.

selected_evidence.snippet: Available data suggest that numerous pathological factors may serve as precipitants for delirium, each having differential effects depending on patient-specific patient physiological characteristics (substrate).

assertion.hypothesis_label: Peripheral inflammation reaching the CNS through a permeable blood-brain barrier
assertion.description: The best-evidenced molecular account of how a systemic insult becomes a brain state. Peripheral pro-inflammatory signalling — IL-6 prominently — is associated with delirium risk before the insult and with delirium severity after it, and the same studies tie the CNS compartment of that signalling to measured blood-brain barrier permeability. Animal work adds the crucial conditional: the same cytokine challenge is cognitively inert in a normal brain and disabling in a degenerating one, which is the vulnerability × precipitant model expressed at the level of a single molecule.

selected_evidence.snippet: Higher preoperative interleukin-6 was associated with postoperative delirium with a standardised mean difference (95% confidence interval) of 0.33 (0.11-0.56) and P=0.003.

Therapeutically, augmenting cholinergic transmission with rivastigmine did not shorten delirium in critically ill patients and the trial was stopped early for excess mortality in the treatment arm; and dopamine-receptor blockade with haloperidol or ziprasidone did not alter delirium duration against placebo. The neurotransmitter disturbance is real and is the best explanation for drug-precipitated delirium; what the negative trials refute is that correcting it downstream reverses the syndrome.

assertion.description: Autoimmune gastritis is initiated by Helicobacter pylori infection via molecular mimicry between H. pylori antigens and the gastric H+/K+ ATPase, generating cross-reactive T- and B-cell responses that, through epitope spreading and bystander activation in a genetically susceptible host, become self-perpetuating autoimmunity and persist after the organism is cleared (established AIG is frequently H. pylori-negative). A corollary is that a subset of cases are reversible with early eradication. Causation in humans remains unproven and is the basis of a knowledge-gap discussion.
assertion.notes: Two independent hypothesis-search runs concur on PARTIALLY SUPPORTED / UNRESOLVED: a claude_code report (kb/hypotheses/Autoimmune_Gastritis/alternative_hpylori_molecular_mimicry_origin/claude_code.md) and a deeper openscientist report (same directory, openscientist.md). H. pylori- to-H+/K+ ATPase cross-reactivity is documented at the T-cell level (cross-reactive gastric CD4 Th1 clones; urease beta-subunit homology; LPS Lewis-antigen mimicry; PMID:14568977), and active, not-yet-atrophic autoimmune corpus gastritis resolved after eradication in 64 of 80 patients in a retrospective, uncontrolled series (PMID:11549834). Neither result reaches the distinctive part of the hypothesis: reversibility achieved while the organism is being cleared is not evidence of a later self-perpetuating "hit-and-run" phase, and epitope spreading and persistence after clearance have no direct human evidence. The model is also refuted at the autoantibody level (antigastric autoantibodies do not absorb to H. pylori; PMID:10738313, PMID:11815766) and is non-general: H. pylori-naive AIG forms a distinct familial/autoimmune-enriched entity (ARIOSO n=1,598; PMID:38976374), and 29.3% of 75 atrophic autoimmune gastritis cases had no reactivity to any of 13 H. pylori antigens on multiplex serology (PMID:41484031). The wider "29-79% H. pylori-naive" range asserted by the openscientist report is not supported - its 21.1% figure was the proportion meeting a stringent multi-antigen positive cutoff, whose complement is not "no evidence of exposure", and its second source is not traceable in the report. Treg-depletion mouse models produce AIG with no infection, and some H. pylori-AIG associations may be inflated by diagnostic misclassification (urease-positive non-H. pylori bacteria overgrowing the achlorhydric stomach, shown in a referral series selected for repeated eradication failure, which cannot quantify bias in the wider literature). Retained ALTERNATIVE, best read as a subset-initiation mechanism whose full initiation-to-persistence sequence is unproven in humans. See the codex assessment sidecar in the hypothesis directory.

assertion.description: The effector arm driving parietal-cell destruction has classically been modeled as Th1/IFN-gamma-polarized, based on murine neonatal-thymectomy and TCR-transgenic effector-transfer systems specific for the H+/K+ ATPase.
assertion.notes: Two independent hypothesis-search runs concur on PARTIALLY SUPPORTED: a claude_code report (kb/hypotheses/Autoimmune_Gastritis/canonical_th1_effector_polarization/claude_code.md) and an openscientist report (same directory, openscientist.md). Both retain Th1/IFN-gamma as foundational and real: human gastric H+/K+ ATPase-reactive CD4 clones are predominantly Th1 and cytotoxic via perforin/Fas-FasL (PMID:11159878, PMID:15763992), and IFN-gamma directly kills murine gastric epithelium in organoids and is required for atrophy and metaplasia in TxA23 mice (PMID:30511397). The causal perturbations are model-specific and are weaker than the openscientist report states: anti-IFN-gamma treatment in the neonatal-thymectomy model cut gastritis incidence from 69% to 16% rather than abolishing disease (PMID:8766575), and in a transfer setting IFN-gamma-deficient T cells could still initiate mild disease (PMID:22777705). Neither run supports a Th1-exclusive model - it is one arm of a cooperative multi-cytokine / multi-cell-type program: CD8 T cells were the dominant IFN-gamma source in that polyclonal mouse model, IFN-gamma plus IL-17 are co-required for severe disease (PMID:22777705), and IL-13 acting through IL-4R-alpha is a separable required arm of the metaplastic transformation - though metaplasia was absent altogether in TxA23 x Ifng-/- mice, so IL-13 independence from IFN-gamma-associated atrophy across the whole trajectory is not established. The codex assessment sidecar in the hypothesis directory rejects two further readings carried by the report: that the PTPN22 pernicious-anemia risk variant wires patients toward Th1 over Th17 (this joins a PA GWAS locus association with Th1/Th17 phenotyping in genotyped healthy donors, and is a hypothesis rather than evidence about gastric polarization; the report also misstates the GWAS p value as 1.91e-10 rather than 1.91e-24), and that a null NK-depletion result rules out innate IFN-gamma sources. The intrinsic-factor-reactive pernicious-anemia compartment is mixed rather than Th17-dominant: the cited 94% is a combined "Th17 or Th1" figure (see emerging_th17_effector_polarization). Caveat: Th1 dominance is demonstrated most robustly in TCR-transgenic / monoclonal systems, which may overrepresent it relative to polyclonal disease, and all human immune data here are cross-sectional, so which effector population dominates over the human disease course is unresolved.

selected_evidence.snippet: Gastric epithelial cells in gastroid cultures expressed IFN-γ receptor in the basolateral membrane, and gastroids died when treated with IFN-γ in an IFN-γ receptor-dependent manner.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Canonical Primary Autoimmunity Against the Gastric H+/K+ ATPase
assertion.description: Autoimmune gastritis is a primary organ-specific autoimmune disease driven by a breakdown of self-tolerance to the parietal-cell H+/K+ ATPase (ATP4A/ATP4B), with CD4 T-cell-mediated parietal cell destruction that clinically tends to progress rather than remit. The tolerance defect implicates the beta subunit: although H/K-ATPase alpha-subunit (ATP4A) mRNA is expressed in the thymus, thymic expression alone does not tolerize the pathogenic T-cell repertoire, and in the murine neonatal-thymectomy system it is the beta subunit (ATP4B), absent from the thymus, whose transgenic thymic expression prevents disease - so ATP4B behaves as the dominant autoantigen in mice. Whether ATP4B-specific T cells likewise dominate the surviving human repertoire, or precede ATP4A reactivity, has not been demonstrated. The murine disease induced by neonatal thymectomy is T-cell-mediated, and monogenic tolerance defects (AIRE/APECED, FOXP3/IPEX) produce autoimmune gastritis as part of polyautoimmunity. Two independent hypothesis-search runs (see notes) concur that this primary/central-tolerance account is best treated as one of several candidate initiating pathways feeding a shared effector cascade, rather than as an infection-independent sole origin.
assertion.notes: Two independent hypothesis-search runs concur on PARTIALLY SUPPORTED: a claude_code report (kb/hypotheses/Autoimmune_Gastritis/canonical_primary_autoimmune_hk_atpase_origin/claude_code.md) and a deeper openscientist report (same directory, openscientist.md; 127 papers, 17 findings over 5 iterations). Both retain the CD4 T-cell / H+/K+ ATPase effector mechanism as CANONICAL but judge the etiological claim of a purely primary, infection-independent origin overstated. Each candidate initiating route is retained only at the evidence level it was actually demonstrated at: primary central-tolerance defect (murine neonatal thymectomy and transgenic thymic ATP4B; PMID:8393475), H. pylori molecular mimicry (human gastric T-cell cross-reactivity only; see alternative_hpylori_molecular_mimicry_origin), neonatal roseolovirus thymic disruption (experimental murine infection; not shown for human roseoloviruses), and peripheral checkpoint failure (anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4 gastritis, supported by deeply phenotyped single cases, which cannot establish absence of host predisposition or identity with sporadic AIG). The codex assessment sidecar in the hypothesis directory rejects three of the openscientist run's stronger readings: that one ATP4A-specific TCR is "necessary and sufficient" (the TxA23 experiment establishes sufficiency only; PMID:11449363), that a prospective progression cohort proves the autoimmune process is mechanistically self-sustaining regardless of trigger (clinical progression is not an immune-mechanism endpoint), and that PTPN22, HLA, ABO and IFIH1 form one confirmed AIG genetic architecture - PTPN22/HLA-DQB1/IL2RA/AIRE come from the pernicious-anemia GWAS (PMID:34145262) while ABO and IFIH1 come from a parietal-cell-antibody GWAS in a type 1 diabetes cohort, a different phenotype and sampling frame. The ATP4A/ATP4B tolerance correction flagged by both runs (alpha thymic expression does not tolerize; ATP4B is the thymus-absent dominant murine autoantigen) has been folded into the description above (PMID:16237067). The report's candidate GO identifiers were not curated: GO:0006968 is cellular defense response, not central tolerance, and GO:0002513 is tolerance induction to self antigen, not a generic peripheral-tolerance term. Follow-up recommended by openscientist: split into separate CANONICAL effector and qualified etiological-trigger hypotheses, and add an upstream "incomplete central tolerance to ATP4B" node.

selected_evidence.snippet: The murine disease induced by neonatal thymectomy is T cell-mediated.

Both retain Th1/IFN-gamma as foundational and real: human gastric H+/K+ ATPase-reactive CD4 clones are predominantly Th1 and cytotoxic via perforin/Fas-FasL (PMID:11159878, PMID:15763992), and IFN-gamma directly kills murine gastric epithelium in organoids and is required for atrophy and metaplasia in TxA23 mice (PMID:30511397). The authors of the mouse study propose testing it in an S102P knock-in.

selected_evidence.snippet: While the recessive mutation is often considered a loss-of-function mutation, it remains possible that the S102P mutation could be a gain-of-function mutation with dose-dependent effects that impair cellular functions.

assertion.hypothesis_label: S102P disturbs GATAD1-dependent chromatin regulation in the heart
assertion.description: The model proposed with the gene discovery: GATAD1 works in an H3K4me3-associated chromatin-regulatory complex, and the variant perturbs cardiac gene expression, as combined loss of the complex partners Hdac1 and Hdac2 does in mouse heart. It is an inference from GATAD1's interaction partners. No GATAD1-dependent cardiac gene set has been measured, and the S102P protein keeps its complex partners in HEK293 cells.

selected_evidence.snippet: While the specific effects of GATAD1-S102P on nucleosome protein interactions and downstream gene expression are unknown, the mutation leads to a heart-specific phenotype and implicates epigenetic dysregulation as a novel basis for human DCM.

assertion.hypothesis_label: G-quadruplex-mediated transcriptional interference at the XDP SVA
assertion.description: The G-rich (CCCTCT)n hexameric repeat within the XDP SVA folds into stable G-quadruplex (G4) structures that interfere with TAF1 transcription. Pharmacologic stabilization of these G4s reduces TAF1 transcripts while destabilization (unfolding) increases TAF1 transcripts, implicating G4 formation as a major cause of aberrant TAF1 expression and a candidate therapeutic target.

selected_evidence.snippet: Our data indicate that G4 formation in the XDP SVA is a major cause of aberrant TAF1 expression

assertion.hypothesis_label: Neostriatal neuronal loss as a driver of dystonia and parkinsonism
assertion.description: Clinicopathologic evidence establishes progressive neostriatal neuronal loss alongside the evolving dystonia-parkinsonism syndrome. A review proposes XDP as a model for studying how striatal neurodegeneration leads to dystonia, but neither that route nor the route to parkinsonism has been experimentally resolved. The associated edges are therefore partial, indirect, and explicitly hypothesis-scoped.

selected_evidence.snippet: XDP may be used as a human disease model to elucidate the pathomechanisms by which striatal neurodegeneration leads to dystonia symptoms.

assertion.hypothesis_label: SVA repeat-RNA and R-loop route to neostriatal neurodegeneration
assertion.description: XDP striatal organoids support a route in which SVA-derived hexamer RNA drives R-loop formation and neuronal injury: SVA deletion ameliorates neurodegenerative readouts, and antisense knockdown of the repeat RNA rescues apoptosis. Whether this model fully explains selective, progressive neuronal loss in the human neostriatum is not yet established.

selected_evidence.snippet: Phenotypic and transcriptomic analysis of XDP and isogenic SVA-deleted striatal organoids reveal that the SVA insertion drives hallmarks of neurodegeneration, including transcriptional dysregulation, decreased neuronal activity, and apoptosis, which are ameliorated by SVA deletion.

assertion.hypothesis_label: TAF1 dysregulation as a route to selective neostriatal neuronal loss
assertion.description: Reduced TAF1 expression is present in patient caudate and is a reproducible SVA-dependent molecular phenotype, but the retained review explicitly says its role in XDP pathogenesis is undefined. The hypothesis therefore records the historically central TAF1 route while leaving its intermediates and its contribution relative to repeat-RNA/R-loop toxicity unresolved.

selected_evidence.snippet: The reduction in the TAF1 expression and the retention of a part of intron 32 in some TAF1 transcripts are currently considered relevant cellular/molecular XDP phenotypes, but their role in XDP pathogenesis is not defined and warrants further investigation.

selected_evidence.snippet: Our endometrial atlas highlights the loss of the endometrial epithelium, alterations to epithelial differentiation signaling pathways such as Wnt and Notch, and the appearance of characteristic epithelium expressing secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor during the window of implantation.

assertion.hypothesis_label: Ferroptotic epithelial stress promotes stromal fibrosis through transferable signals
